page: Microsoft Azure M64ds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor, this configuration delivers 64 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 1024.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is designed for memory-bound enterprise systems requiring expansive working memory alongside consistent core compute capacity.

Storage configuration includes 2199 GB of local SSD capacity, along with architectural support for Premium Storage. The local solid-state storage provides fast temporary scratch space and swap functionality, while the system operates without onboard discrete GPU accelerators. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the virtual machine allocation.

From an efficiency standpoint, the M64ds_v2 concentrates high memory density into a single virtualized host, reducing the operational overhead associated with clustering smaller instances. The absence of graphical hardware and unnecessary compute sprawl maximizes host resources strictly for memory and local I/O performance. This profile fits large-scale relational databases, in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning suites, and high-throughput data processing engines.
